what: vLLM's TTFT Over Time and ITL Over Time panels during a request-rate ramp
provenance: replayed from measured/ch03/vllm-ramp.om.gz (vLLM 0.29.0 CPU backend on the reference laptop, 2026-09-19)
caption: vLLM 0.29.0's TTFT Over Time and ITL Over Time panels in Grafana 13.2.2, replayed from measured/ch03/: a request-rate ramp on the CPU backend of the reference laptop.
notes: Both panels come from vLLM 0.29.0's Performance Statistics dashboard, print-patched for line style and colour only.

Grafana's datasource step is 15 s here. vLLM's Performance Statistics panels use rate(...[$__interval]) rather than $__rate_interval, so a step equal to the lab's 5-second scrape interval puts one sample in the window and the panels return nothing; 15 s is three samples. The lab's own queries (measured/ch03/promql.json) are evaluated at the same 15-second step.
The TTFT panel's clock starts at the engine; the ITL panel is chunk-level, not a per-request TPOT.

Grafana's 'Powered by Grafana' embed watermark, which sits over the plot in the top-right corner and cannot be switched off in the OSS build, was removed from the DOM before the shot. Nothing else on the panel was changed.

what: llama.cpp's built-in web UI streaming an answer on the reference laptop

steps.text: What is a token, and why is a language model billed by the token? Answer in three sentences.

provenance: live on the reference laptop: llama.cpp v0.4.1 (build b10964) serving SmolLM2-135M-Instruct Q8_0 on the CPU
caption: llama.cpp v0.4.1's built-in web UI mid-answer, SmolLM2-135M-Instruct Q8_0 on the reference laptop's CPU, 2026-09-20: the model, the token counts and the tokens per second are all local.
notes: MEASURED on the reference laptop (Apple M2 Pro, 16 GB, CPU only). Every number on the screen is this laptop's and belongs to no GPU.
The frame is one where the stop control was up both before and after the screenshot, so the answer really is mid-stream; nothing is staged and no text is edited.

The tokens-per-second the UI shows for the answer is computed over elapsed wall time and this frame is taken part-way through, so it sits below the completed-request figure chapter 1 reports for the same model.
llama.cpp caches prompts between requests, so screens/live-servers.sh starts a fresh server for the capture; a re-run against a warm server reports a one-token prefill and a nonsense prefill rate.

what: GuideLLM's HTML report, the TTFT and throughput charts of the sweep
css:

svg { overflow: visible !important; }
provenance: measured/ch04/guidellm.html, the report GuideLLM 0.7.4 wrote for the sweep against vLLM 0.29.0's CPU backend on the reference laptop, 2026-09-19
caption: GuideLLM 0.7.4's own report for the sweep in measured/ch04/: time to first token and throughput against achieved rate, vLLM 0.29.0 CPU backend on the reference laptop, 2026-09-19.
notes: MEASURED on the reference laptop's CPU backend. Where this curve bends is set by that CPU and says nothing about where a GPU's bends.

GuideLLM 0.7.4's report ships dark-only: it has no light theme and ignores prefers-color-scheme, so this is the one capture in the book that is not on a white ground. Inverting it would have shown the reader a report that does not exist.

Print patches, and nothing else (screens/guidellm-print.js): the chart's SVG type is raised from 10 px to 14 px, the rotated y-axis title is slid clear of the wider tick labels, and each of the five series gets a line style, because p50, p90, p95, p99 and the mean are otherwise told apart by colour alone. No colour, number, axis or data point is changed.

what: the $/M output-token recording rule, over a simulator driven at chapter 5's cited rate
provenance: simulated at a cited rate: llm-d-inference-sim v0.11.2 paced to MLPerf v6.1 Server's 89,856.3 output tokens a second for one eight-B200 node, with ch15/cost.yml backfilled over it
caption: Simulated at a cited rate: ch15/cost.yml over llm-d-inference-sim v0.11.2 paced to MLPerf's 89,856.3 output tokens a second for one node, so the panel reads chapter 5's $0.177 per million; Grafana 13.2.2.
notes: SIMULATED, and the delicate one. Not one token here was produced by the reference laptop's engine, and no laptop rate is multiplied by a GPU price. The simulator was paced to a PUBLISHED per-node output-token rate (MLPerf Inference v6.1 Server, eight B200s), so the rule divides chapter 5's dated list price by chapter 5's cited throughput and returns chapter 5's own figure.

The laptop's Prometheus never loads this rule -- ch15/prometheus.yml has two rule files, not three -- for exactly the reason the chapter gives. Here the rule is evaluated by promtool tsdb create-blocks-from rules over the simulator's counter, never over a lab's.
screens/cost_pacer.py held the counter on the cited line to within 109 ms of generation; the achieved rate over the 780-second recording was 89,844.3 tokens a second, 99.99% of the cited figure.
